What is the postcode of the address we have for you?

intents.hardship: Financial hardship (job loss, illness, cannot cover essentials).
intents.dispute: "This isn't my debt" or "I never had that product".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan or lower instalments.
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

lines.opening: Hello, this is Isla, a digital assistant calling from Glenmorrow Savings Bank. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I'm Isla, a digital assistant calling from Glenmorrow Savings Bank.
lines.scam: I understand your caution. I'm calling from Glenmorrow Savings Bank, and I will never ask for your PIN or passwords.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can explain once I've confirmed I'm speaking with the right person. May I ask you two quick security questions?
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share any details until I've confirmed who I'm speaking with.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand, and I'll keep this brief.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {title} {last_name}?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, I can only call back between 9 am and 6:30 pm, today or on the next two business days. Is there another time that works?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss this with {title} {last_name}.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you. We'll call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry for the trouble, and thank you for letting me know.
lines.condolence: I'm very sorry for your loss.
lines.id_intro: Before we go on, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_why: We ask these questions to protect your personal information and make sure we only speak with you.
lines.id_explain: It's a quick check to keep your information safe, and I can't go on without it.
lines.id_declined: I understand. Without these answers I can't go any further today.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that doesn't match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I can't continue with this call. Please visit a branch or log in to online banking.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you, {first_name}. I'm calling about overdue payments.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} in arrears, and it is {days} days overdue.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full {amount} today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay both amounts in full today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. Could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't record an amount that low. The least I can accept is {floor}. Could you pay {floor}?
lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, that's still below the amount I can accept.
lines.date_past: That date has already passed. Could you choose a date from today onwards?
lines.not_business_day: That's not a business day. The next business day is {date}. Would that work?
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, the latest date I can accept is {date}. Could you pay by then?
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day would that be?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: To repeat, that's {amount} on {date}. Would that work for you?
lines.readback_intro: Let me read that back to you.
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can accept is {deadline}, so I've used that date.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise has been recorded.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, your promise for the {name} could not be recorded.
lines.paid_line: Thank you. Payments can take two business days to show, so I won't ask you for a payment on this one.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I won't ask you for a payment on this one.
lines.hardship: I'm sorry to hear you're going through this. I'm passing you to our care team, who can help.
lines.hardship_short: Shall I put you through now?
lines.restructure_line: I'm passing you to our arrears solutions team, who can talk to you about payment plans.
lines.human_ask_help: I can help with most things on this call. Would you like me to try first?
lines.transfer: Please hold while I transfer you.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change that promise on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {amount}.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book that callback.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer didn't go through.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Do you confirm, yes or no?
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our system isn't responding right now.

assumptions: The memo of 19 October 2026 overrides policy v3.2 where they differ, as the email and the memo both say. The old dialler code list was not updated for the memo, so the memo also wins over it.

Bands follow memo A: early is 1-14 days, mid is 15-30 and late is 31-60. Deadlines and attempts per band are unchanged: early = 8th business day after today (today not counted), 1 attempt; mid = today + 14 calendar days, 2 attempts; late = last business day of the current month, 3 attempts.
Calendar follows memo B: Friday 11 December 2026 is added as a non-business day alongside the bank holidays in rule 11. 24 December 2026 stays a business day.
Codes follow memo C: the reason 'refused' is replaced by 'declined' for both the close_call reason and the add_note reason. The tool API enums confirm this.

Callback window follows memo D: 09:00 to 18:30, both included. Allowed days are today or the next two business days, and the time must be later than now. business_days_only is true because calls are only placed on business days and memo B bans callbacks on 11 December.

The floor stays at 30% of arrears_amount, rounded up to the next whole pound. A result that is already a whole number of pounds is not rounded further (rule 17, confirmed by the memo). If the rounded floor is more than arrears_amount (only possible below about £1.43), the floor is capped at arrears_amount. The brief does not cover this case.
monthly_payment is never used or quoted.
get_account gives amounts in pounds (amount_scale 1). create_promise takes amount_pence, so promise_scale is 100.
Late-band rollover (rule 14): if today is already the last business day of the month, the deadline is the last business day of next month (roll_if_not_after_today).
Mid-band deadlines that fall on a weekend or holiday move to the business day before (deadline_adjust previous_business_day). The other band deadlines already fall on business days.

Ladder (rule 20): step 1 is the full amount today, and the opening ask counts as attempt 1. Step 2 is the full amount on the 5th business day after today, or on the deadline if that is earlier. The ladder cannot express 'whichever is earlier', so this assumes the engine clamps every proposed date to the product's deadline. Step 3 is the floor on the deadline.

Rule 21: if the customer says the full amount is too much, the next step offers the floor on that step's date (full_or_floor on step 2). Attempts never go past the band's limit, so in the early band the opening ask uses the only attempt.
first_ask is 'today' (rule 16: always ask for the full amount first, and step 1 is today). With two products, a flat no to 'both in full today' counts as step 1 for each product (rule 23).
Notes are on (rule 25). No notes are written on any transfer (rule 29), so hardship has no note.

Hardship (rule 28) is a direct transfer to care_team, closed as handoff/care. The customer is told about the transfer, not offered it. hardship_short and hardship_declined are filled in only because the format requires them.
Request for a person: the agent asks once whether Isla can help, then transfers to customer_care (handoff/human). Payment-plan request: transfer to arrears_solutions (handoff/restructure).

The verify_identity date_of_birth answer is sent as DDMMYYYY (%d%m%Y). The postcode is sent in capitals with one space before the last three characters. No fixed postcode length is set because UK postcodes vary in length.
The identity check ends after 2 wrong answers in total across both questions (rule 9, confirmed by the memo). A refusal gets one explanation, and a second refusal closes as id_fail/declined_id.

The verify_identity response has no hint field (its fields are ok, error, verified, wrong_answers_left, all_verified), so identity.response.hint is empty and hints is empty. Unreadable answers come back as ok=false and are not counted.
The brief does not define 'next <weekday>', so the default 'following_week' is used.
confirm max_asks is 2: an answer still unclear after a second ask closes as no_contact/unclear.
Texting a payment link was dropped (per the email), so sms_line is empty. The brief gives no rule for changing a recorded promise, so the agent says it cannot be changed on this call.
The brief prescribes no confirmation wording beyond 'one clear yes', so 'Is that correct?' is used.
Defaults kept because the brief says nothing: ask_anything_else after a promise, max_not_talk 2, clamp_single_date true, purpose_is_decline true.
The opening says 'We record this call' to meet rule 2, which requires saying that the call is recorded.
Every product's days_in_arrears falls in a band (scope is 1-60), so bands_outside is null.
